issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` may match non-time tokens in identifiers/strings
issues.detail: The early-exit guard tests the raw declaration value with `/\dm?s/i`. This will match things like `1s` inside a string literal, a url, or an ident such as `grid-area: span1s` (contrived but legal). For a perf short-circuit that's fine since the real parser still runs on any match, but it is technically broader than 'has a time token'. Worth a one-line comment noting this is a deliberately loose pre-filter for the parser, not a validator.

issues.description: Changeset message could state the why, not just the what
issues.detail: `Fixed: time-min-milliseconds performance` is accurate but thin. Two more words ('avoid parsing declarations without a time token') would tell the next maintainer why this diff exists without making them open the PR. Not a blocker.

review.summary: Three-line patch that short-circuits `walkDecls` when the value can't possibly contain a time token. Diff is scoped, readable, matches the surrounding style, and moves the `propertyName` computation below the guard so the cheap path is actually cheap. This is what a perf fix should look like — small, obvious, and the next maintainer won't curse anyone. Regex is a loose pre-filter rather than a strict matcher, which is the right call for a guard but deserves a one-line comment. ACCEPT.
